caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.143 of 2019
lawyer:
Mr. Sheikh Mohammad Murshed, Additional Attorney General instructed by Ms. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record --------- For the Petitioner 
Mr. Sadhan Kumar Banik, Advocate-on-Record -------- For the Respondent
parties:
The State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong -------- Petitioner
-Vs-
Md Mehedi Alam --- Respondent
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This criminal petition i for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 26th day of November, 2018 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.45905 of 2015 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The facts relevant to dispose of the case are that one Md. Osman Gani, Sub-Inspector of Police of Bondar Police Station, Chittagong, lodged First Information Report (FIR) with Bondar Police Station, Chittagong alleging, inter-alia, that accused Md. Golam Mostafa (39) (who has been arrested under section 54 of the Penal Code on the basis of a GDE being No.344 dated 08.06.2015) and Nur Mohammad along with other unknown accused imported banned drugs/cocaine in container without opening any LC in the name of shipping agent named COSCO Bangladesh Shipping Lines, 2/F, HRC Bhaban, 64-66 Agrabad Commercial Area and thereby have com-mitted offence under section 19(1) of Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990. 

 4. The aforesaid First Information Report (FIR) was registered as Bondar Police Station Case No.22 dated 27.06.2015 for commissioning the offence punishable under Table 1 (Kha) of section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbo Niyantron AM, 1990. 

 5. The accused-respondent filed an application seeking bail in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong in connection with Bondar Police Station Case No.22 dated 27.06.2015 corresponding to GR No.117 of 2015 under Table 1(Kha) of section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong rejected the bail petition. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order of rejection of bail by the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, the accused-respondent preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.45905 of 2015 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division after hearing both the sides made the Rule absolute and granted bail by the judgment and order dated 26.11.2018. 

 8. Mr. Sheikh Mohammad Murshed, learned Additional Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute clearly shows non-application of judicial mind having failed to appreciate that there is strong prima facie and specific overt act of committing heinous offence under Table 1(Kha) of section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain,1990 which had come at one stage of investigation that the instant accused-respondent in connivance with each other imported huge quantity of cocaine in the name of 'Sunflower Oil' without LC and BL consignment. He further submits that co-accused, Md. Golam Mostafa alias Shohel and Mostafa Kamal made inculpatory confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of the Criminal Procedure narrating their involvement in details regarding the alleged imported cocaine without LC/BL consignment in the name of Sun-flower Oil. He lastly submits that in the instant case, the investigation is going on, at this stage, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute will create hindrance in the way of free and fair investigation. 

 9. Mr. Sadhan Kumar Banik, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the respondent, made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He adds that the respondent made no confession in the instant case and this respondent is not at all bound by the confessions made by the other co-accused. 

 11. On perusal of the record, it appears that investigation of the case is going on against the accused-respondent, Md. Mehedi Alam for commission of offence punishable under section 19(1) 9(Kha) of Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990 read with section 258 of the Special Power Act, 1974. It appears from the First Information Report (FIR) that the First Information Report (FIR) named accused No.1, Golam Mostafa and No.2, Md. Nur Mohammad and others have committed the offence under the provisions of Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990 by way of illegally importing cocaine in two containers, each having a capacity of 185 K.G. These two containers are part of the consignment of the 'Sun-flower Oil' imported from Bolivia in 107 containers. The cocaine was detected by the Customs Officials before clearance of the consignment. The containers bear the writing showing its number as "JP 094717 and JP 09427" and the expression COSCO. All the 107 containers were seized by the informant in terms of a seizure list. The learned Judges of the Division Bench made the Rule absolute and there by enlarged the accused-respondent, Md. Mehedi Alam, son of late Dr. Nasir Uddin on bail in the case on furnishing bail bond subject to the satisfaction of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 12. On completion of investigation, Police submitted once charge sheet and one supplementary charge sheet with a recommendation to stand trial of a number of persons including the prosecution of the accused-petitioner under the Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990. It also transpires that the said police reports were not accepted by the Court concerned and the case is still under further investigation. 

 13. The learned Additional Attorney General argued that the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute clearly shows non-application of judicial mind having failed to appreciate that there is strong prima facie case and specific overt act of committing heinous offence under Table 1 (Kha) of section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990 which had come at one stage of investigation that the instant accused-respondent in connivance with each other imported huge quantity of cocaine in the name of 'Sun-flower Oil' without LC and BL consignment and that co-accused, Md. Golam Mostafa alias Shohel and Mostafa Kamal made inculpatory confessional statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure narrating their involvement in details regarding the alleged imported cocaine without LC/BL consignment in the name of sunflower oil. 

 14. On the other hand, that the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-respondent argued that the accused-petitioner is an employee of a Securities Company. He is not First Information Report (FIR) named. He has been arrested on suspicion and that the further investigation report is yet to receive and there is no possibility of sub-mitting police report in the case in near future. 

 15. It appears from the record that this is a case under section 19(1)9(Kha) of the Madak Drobbo Niyantron Ain, 1990. Though the name of this accused-petitioner is not figured in the First Information Report (FIR), but this is a case of recovery of huge quantity of cocaine. The offence is very grieve. The police for-warding speaks that evidence is forthcoming against this accused-petitioner. It appears that accuse- Golam Mustafa @ Shohel a cousin of this respondent and another co-accused admitted their guilt by making a confessional statement which appears to be inculpatory in nature. Not only that, this respondent also made an inculpatory statement wherein he admitted that main exporter F'z1u is his cousin who at first made correspondence with him regarding this export and clearance of such consignment. All the confessing accused made confession involving this respondent. Huge quantity of cocaine was recovered by the Custom Officials before clearance of the consignment and the containers bear the writing as has been shown its number "JP 094717 and JP 09427" and the expression COSCO, as it appears from the First Information Report (FIR), seizure list and confessional statements. Furthermore, further investigation is going on, it is expected that the police will submit such report within a short while. At this stage, it will not be wise to enlarge the petitioner on bail. Thus, the criminal petition for the leave to appeal is disposed of. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. Stay granted earlier by the Chamber Judge is to be continued.
